paper_id: Li and Liu - 2007 - Underground structure monitoring with wireless sensor networks
title: Underground Structure Monitoring with Wireless Sensor Networks
motivation: Coal mine collapses cause 50%+ of 480 fatalities in US; rapid detection of collapse holes is critical for rescue
problem_framing: Detect hole regions via neighbor loss in mesh network; maintain system validity when topology suddenly changes
key_insight: No accelerometers needed—exploit the sensor node hole itself as the indicator of collapse location
method_signature: Hexagonal mesh deployment + beacon mechanism + convex hull of edge nodes to bound hole region
evaluation_criteria: Detection error (m), reconfiguration error (2D/3D), processing latency, packet loss rate
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: RSS-based neighbor detection fails in coal mine due to dynamic signals; single-node holes undetectable
evidence_for_taste: a naïve method...failed in our prototype
a small hole affecting only one sensor node cannot be detected
such a centralized approach often suffers long latency
directly employing those approaches...will lead to poor detection accuracy
thinking_moves: 把传感检测问题重新定义为网络拓扑变化问题
用网络连通性替代传感器硬件检测
先证明凸包定理成立, 再以此作为检测误差上界
通过hexagonal规则部署消除邻居集合的不确定性
extraction_notes: Full paper available with complete method and evaluation sections. Authors clearly distinguish their work from existing WSN hole detection by NOT relying on accelerometers and NOT assuming stable network topology.
